Chapter 6: The Legacy of Culture—How History Shapes Habits.
Have you ever noticed how the way people act today is often a mirror of what came before? Culture isn’t just about the food we eat, the languages we speak, or the holidays we celebrate.
It’s a web of habits, beliefs, and expectations that get handed down—sometimes so quietly, we barely notice. These invisible threads? They tug at our choices every day, shaping how we deal with challenges and grab hold of opportunities.
Imagine a busy office, filled with all kinds of personalities. Some folks jump right in during meetings, eager to share ideas or question a decision. Others? They hang back, thinking things through, maybe a little hesitant to challenge the boss. It’s tempting to chalk this up to just personality differences, but there’s usually something deeper at play.
The way we talk to those in charge, how we handle mistakes, even how we speak up—all of it can be traced back to the culture we grew up in.
Let me tell you a story. Picture a pilot and co-pilot flying through rough skies. The co-pilot spots a problem, but hesitates—worried about stepping out of line. That tiny pause almost leads to disaster. It wasn’t about skill or smarts; it was about a culture where respecting authority is everything. Now, in another part of the world, the same situation unfolds. This time, the co-pilot doesn’t wait—he speaks up, and they avert the crisis. The real difference? The legacy of culture.
These patterns aren’t just found in the cockpit. You’ll see them everywhere—from classrooms to boardrooms. In some places, questioning a teacher or your boss is a good thing. In others, it’s seen as disrespect. Over time, these habits decide who gets heard, who gets ahead, and who’s willing to take risks. Most people never realize how much the past shapes what they do—or how tough it can be to break out of those old routines.
But here’s the good news. Once you recognize how much culture influences you, you can start to change it. You can build workplaces or classrooms where everyone feels safe to speak up, where fresh ideas are welcomed, and where the best solutions have a real chance to shine.
It’s not easy, but it’s possible. And it all begins by paying attention to the stories and habits we each carry with us.
